title: Tech World Rallies Behind Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as Reinstatement Petition Top 100K Signatures
snippet: Tech leaders including Elon Musk and thousands of Nvidia employees are urging the board to grant former CEO Jensen Huang due process following his sudden resignation amid personal scandals and espionage inquiries.
content:
A growing chorus of Silicon Valley heavyweights and Nvidia employees are demanding the reinstatement of long-time chief executive Jensen Huang, following his abrupt resignation earlier this week. A grassroots campaign dubbed "Stand with Jensen" has garnered over 108,000 signatures, calling on Nvidia's board of directors to grant the co-founder due process standard for a leader who spent more than three decades shaping the semiconductor giant.

High-profile tech figures—including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad—have publicly backed the campaign. According to petition organizers, the signers include more than 5,600 current Nvidia employees and over 58,000 shareholders who view Huang's leadership as essential to the company's unique culture and technological dominance.

Resignation Amid Foreign Intelligence Inquiries

Huang stepped down on Thursday after admitting to personal affairs, including one with an Nvidia executive. The move came shortly after Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation. Previous reporting pointed to a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, who U.S. intelligence officials suspect may have ties to Chinese espionage—an allegation China has denied.

Following Huang's departure, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. However, organizers of the reinstatement campaign argue the board acted hastily without disclosing clear evidence or affording Huang a fair opportunity to defend himself against espionage allegations.

Internal Pushback and Investor Concerns

Support for Huang extends deep inside Nvidia's ranks. Internal employee message boards have seen thousands of comments rallying behind the former CEO, with workers comparing his visionary leadership to that of Steve Jobs. While employees acknowledge the need to investigate potential code-of-conduct violations, many insist the board should preserve a pathway for his return if espionage claims prove unsubstantiated.

Prominent institutional investors have also weighed in. Executives at Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management sent a joint letter to Nvidia's board on Friday, cautioning against a rushed leadership transition and urging directors to take a measured approach that serves the company's long-term interests—even if that means bringing Huang back to the helm.
